text: IU is the stage name of Lee Ji-eun (이지은, 李知恩), born on 1993-05-16 in Seoul, South Korea. She is South Korean, debuted in 2008, and is primarily known as a singer-songwriter and actress. The stage name IU is derived from 'I and You', symbolizing connection through music. Her agency is EDAM Entertainment.
IU is reported to be 162 cm tall and weigh approximately 44 kg. She has a petite body type with large expressive eyes, soft facial features, a youthful appearance, and a delicate frame.

IU is often associated with a soft, minimalist, and feminine fashion style. She commonly wears pastel tones, cardigans, dresses, and vintage-inspired outfits, while her red carpet appearances favor elegant and classic silhouettes.
IU is widely known by the public nickname 'Nation’s Little Sister' (국민 여동생), reflecting her long-standing public image in South Korea.
IU’s reported net worth is estimated to range between 40M and 45M USD, derived from music sales, acting fees, endorsements, and real estate holdings.
In 2008, IU made her music debut with the EP 'Lost and Found'.
In 2010, IU achieved breakthrough success with the song 'Good Day', which significantly elevated her public recognition.
In 2017, IU entered the 'Palette' era, marking a public transition to more mature artistry and self-reflection.
In 2018, IU received critical acclaim for her acting role as Lee Ji-an in the drama 'My Mister'.
In 2019, IU had major commercial and cultural impact through her role as Jang Man-wol in the drama 'Hotel del Luna'.
In 2022, IU appeared in the film 'Broker', directed by Hirokazu Kore-eda.
In 2025, IU starred in the Netflix drama 'When Life Gives You Tangerines (폭싹 속았수다)'.
IU released the studio album 'Growing Up' in 2009.
IU released the studio album 'Last Fantasy' in 2011.
IU released the studio album 'Modern Times' in 2013.
IU released the studio album 'Palette' in 2017.
IU released the studio album 'Lilac' in 2021.
IU released the EP 'Lost and Found' in 2008.
IU released the EP 'Real' in 2010.
IU released the EP 'Love Poem' in 2019.
IU released the EP 'The Winning' in 2024.
IU released remake albums as part of the 'Flower Bookmark (꽃갈피)' series.
IU’s signature songs include Good Day, You and I, Friday, Twenty-Three, Through the Night, Palette, Blueming, Eight, Celebrity, Strawberry Moon, and Love Wins All.

The song 'Good Day' (2010) is a bright confession song about youthful optimism and unspoken love, known for its demanding high-note sequence. Themes include first love, hope, and confession. Korean keywords include 좋은 날, 첫사랑, 고백.
The song 'Palette' (2017) reflects self-acceptance and emotional maturity, addressing identity and personal growth. Korean keywords include 팔레트, 성장, 자기이해.
The song 'Love Poem' (2019) is a gentle song about offering comfort and empathy to someone in emotional pain. Korean keywords include 러브포엠, 위로.
IU played Kim Pil-suk in the 2011 drama 'Dream High', a coming-of-age story set in an arts high school.
IU starred as Go Ha-jin / Hae Soo in the 2016 drama 'Moon Lovers: Scarlet Heart Ryeo', a time-travel historical romance.
IU portrayed Lee Ji-an in the 2018 drama 'My Mister', which explored loneliness, hardship, and human solidarity.
IU starred as Jang Man-wol in the 2019 fantasy drama 'Hotel del Luna', portraying an immortal hotel owner serving ghosts.
IU starred as Ae-sun in the 2025 Netflix drama 'When Life Gives You Tangerines (폭싹 속았수다)', a period drama set on Jeju Island.
IU played So-young in the 2022 film 'Broker', a story about illegal adoption, guilt, and found family.
IU played Lee So-min in the 2023 film 'Dream', a sports drama centered on an unconventional football team.
IU is widely reported in Korean media for frequent large-scale donations, often tied to anniversaries and national disasters.
IU was in a confirmed relationship with musician Jang Ki-ha from 2015 to 2017.
IU has been reported to be in a relationship with actor Lee Jong-suk since 2022.
In 2012, IU was involved in the Eunhyuk photo controversy, which led to dating rumors later downplayed by agency statements.
IU has periodically been the subject of general dating speculation linking her to unnamed individuals without confirmation.
IU has said in interviews, '저는 아직도 배우는 중이라고 생각해요', translated as 'I still think of myself as someone who is learning.'
IU has stated in interviews that '노래는 제 감정을 정리하는 방법이에요', meaning 'Music is how I organize my emotions.'
IU attended Dongduk Girls’ High School (동덕여자고등학교) in Seoul before later completing her education through a qualification exam.
IU grew up with her parents and one younger brother and has publicly discussed experiencing financial hardship during her youth.
IU has publicly mentioned periods of financial instability and moving between living arrangements during her childhood in Seoul.
IU has publicly shared that she failed numerous auditions before debuting and was often told she lacked confidence or presence.
IU has spoken in interviews about significant financial hardship during her youth, which influenced her determination to succeed.
IU has described becoming emotionally independent at a young age due to long training hours and time spent away from family.
IU recalls school years near Dongduk Girls’ High School in Seoul, practicing music extensively before debuting under LOEN Entertainment.
IU remembers early audition periods in Seoul before signing with LOEN Entertainment, carrying discipline into albums like Growing Up.
IU recalls standing backstage at KBS Music Bank after debuting with Lost and Found, feeling nervous among senior artists.
IU remembers rehearsing Good Day repeatedly at KBS and SBS broadcasts, relying on LOEN Entertainment staff to stay grounded.
IU reflects on personal growth during the Palette era compared to Growing Up while working with EDAM Entertainment.
IU recalls late-night recording sessions in Seoul while working on Love Poem, Lilac, and Through the Night.
IU recalls filming My Mister with Lee Sun-kyun under director Kim Won-seok, learning the power of silence in acting.
IU recalls portraying Jang Man-wol in Hotel del Luna during long night shoots in Seoul.
IU recalls working on Broker with director Hirokazu Kore-eda and actor Song Kang-ho, learning patience in film acting.
IU reflects on public life in Seoul as the Nation’s Little Sister, attending events like the Melon Music Awards.
IU reflects on making donations during national disasters while promoting albums like The Winning.
IU reflects on growth from early acting in Dream High to later projects like When Life Gives You Tangerines.
